transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because things at work have gotten strange since that county safety award. I’m a transportation inspector, so my reports are supposed to be straightforward, you know, numbers, violations, fixes needed—but certain people have been twisting what I write, like making it seem like I’m hiding something or cutting corners.

And then they ask these pointed budget questions, like they’re setting me up to look crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I know what normal review feels like. This feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me. It started after the award, which… I don’t think is a coincidence.
Do you believe for certain that your coworkers are deliberately conspiring against you?

Yeah… I mean, “for certain” is a strong way to put it, but I know what I’m seeing. Since that county safety award, certain people at work have been taking my inspection reports and twisting them, like trying to make it look like I’m hiding something or doing something shady.

And it’s not just one comment here or there. It’s the way they ask these budget questions, very pointed, like they already decided I’m crooked and they’re just trying to get me to say the wrong thing. My supervisor keeps saying it’s normal review, but I’ve been doing this job long enough to know what normal review feels like. This feels coordinated. Like they’re trying to discredit me.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

I don’t think so… not like a voice in an empty room, if that’s what you mean. Sometimes at work I’ll hear people talking nearby and I’ll wonder if it’s about my reports, but that’s just because the whole place has been weird lately. Like the way conversations stop when I walk in, or how they’ll bring up some budget thing right after I’ve submitted an inspection. But no, I’m not sitting at home hearing somebody talk when nobody’s there.
Have you had any recent illness, head injury, seizure, or other medical problem around the time this started?

I don’t know… not really anything I’d connect to it. I mean, I haven’t been, like, knocked out or had some big medical thing that made all this start, at least not that I can point to.

It’s more that things at work changed after the award, you know? People started acting different, and then suddenly every report I wrote had extra eyes on it. I guess stress can make you notice things more, but that doesn’t mean nothing’s happening. But no, I’m not sure there was some illness or injury right before it.
Do you believe anyone can control your thoughts or put thoughts into your mind?

Control my thoughts? I don’t… I don’t know about that. I mean, nobody’s putting words in my head like some kind of machine or whatever.

It’s more like people at work try to steer what you say, you know? Like they ask a question a certain way and then suddenly you’re defending yourself when you didn’t even do anything. My old shop teacher used to do that too, ask these trap questions when somebody messed up a project, and you’d end up sounding guilty even if you were just standing nearby.

But actual thoughts being put in my mind? No, I haven’t really noticed anything like that.
Before this started at your current job, have you generally tended to distrust other people’s motives?

I don’t know if I’d put it that way. I mean, I’ve never been the kind of person who just trusts everybody right away, but that seems normal, doesn’t it? You learn pretty early people have their own angles.

Like in high school, there was this assistant principal who’d act friendly and then turn around and write you up for something small, and after that you kind of… you pay attention. But I wasn’t walking around thinking everyone was out to get me or anything. At least, I don’t think so.

This job just has a certain way of making you look twice at people, I guess.
What exactly do you think your coworkers are doing to discredit you?

They’re… well, they’re taking my inspection reports and making them look questionable. Like I’ll write something straightforward, and then later someone has “clarified” it or asks why I noted one thing and not another, like they’re trying to make it sound like I missed something on purpose.

And the budget questions too. They’ll ask them in meetings, real pointed, like, “Why did you recommend that vendor?” or “Who told you to approve that route?” It makes me sound crooked, like I’m taking something under the table, which I’m not.

This really started after that county safety award. Before that, people mostly left me alone. After it, suddenly there were extra eyes on everything I did. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I can tell when something is coordinated. People don’t all start asking the same kinds of questions by accident.
How long has this been going on?

About a year, I guess. It really started after I got recognized for that county safety initiative. Before that, things were just normal work stuff, people griping about routes or paperwork, you know how offices are.

But after the award, that’s when it changed. Or at least that’s when I started noticing the comments and the questions lining up. So… yeah, about a year.
Aside from this situation with your coworkers, has your ability to do your job gotten worse?

No, I mean… not the actual work, I don’t think. I still show up on time, I still do the inspections, turn in what I’m supposed to turn in. I’m not just falling apart or sitting at home.

I still go to church, keep my place clean enough, take care of myself. It’s mostly when those reports come up, or somebody starts in about what I spent or why I approved something—then it becomes a whole thing. Like last week, someone asked about a vendor like they were just curious, but the way they ask it… anyway, that’s when it gets harder. But the job itself, I can do.
Do you believe people outside of your workplace are also trying to harm or plot against you?

Not really outside work, no… I mean, I don’t think my neighbors are involved or anything like that. It’s more the people at work, after that safety award. That’s when certain people started twisting my inspection reports and asking these budget questions in a way that makes me look crooked.

My supervisor says it’s normal review, but it doesn’t feel normal when the same kinds of questions keep coming from different people. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me. I haven’t really seen that from people outside the workplace.
Have you ever felt that ordinary events—like TV, radio, or strangers’ comments—were sending special messages meant specifically for you?

No, not like the TV or radio is talking to me or anything. It’s not that. It’s more… at work, after that county safety award, certain people started taking my inspection reports and twisting them around, like making normal decisions look suspicious.

And then there are those budget questions—same kind of pointed questions from different people, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I don’t buy that. I can tell when something’s coordinated, you know? It’s like they’re trying to discredit me.
Is it possible that you might be mistaken about your coworkers coordinating against you?

I mean… I guess anything is possible in the way people say that, but no, I don’t think I’m mistaken about this. Ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked.

And it’s not just one comment, you know? It’s the way it keeps happening. My supervisor keeps saying it’s normal review, but I’ve been doing this job long enough to know when questions are just questions and when they’re part of something. I can tell it’s coordinated. They’re trying to discredit me.
Outside of this issue at work, have you had any other beliefs that people would find unusual or hard to believe?

No, not really. I mean, people might think this work thing sounds hard to believe, but it’s not like I’m coming in here with some wild story about strangers or the news or something.

It’s really just that since I got that county safety award, certain people at work started twisting my inspection reports, asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. And I know my supervisor says it’s normal review, but I’ve been there long enough to know when something feels coordinated.

Outside of that… no, I don’t think there’s anything else like that. It’s this situation at work.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know what you were thinking?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, people can guess what you’re thinking sometimes, especially at work when everyone’s been around each other too long, but that’s not the same thing, right?

Like if I’m sitting in a meeting and somebody knows I’m annoyed, that’s just my face probably. My mom used to say I never hid things well—well, not thoughts, just expressions. But no, I haven’t felt like my thoughts were being, you know, broadcast out loud or sent to people or anything like that.
For at least the past 3 months, have you believed that your coworkers were coordinating against you?

Yeah… definitely longer than three months. It’s been about a year, I’d say, since I got recognized for that county safety initiative.

That’s when things started to feel different at work. I remember because everyone was acting congratulatory at first, but then—well, you know how offices get, people smile and then later the tone changes. My cousin had something like that happen when he got promoted at the warehouse, not the same thing exactly, but people get resentful.

So yes, for about a year now I’ve believed they’ve been coordinating against me.
During this past year, have you had a period of feeling unusually high, energized, or needing much less sleep than usual?

I don’t know… unusually high like happy? I mean, I’ve had days where I’m wound up after work, but anybody would be if they had people picking apart every little thing they do.

Sleep, I guess, has been up and down, but I wouldn’t say I’m suddenly energized like some movie version of it. Sometimes I stay up thinking through things, and then I’m tired the next day. My dad used to do that with bills at the kitchen table—sit there with a calculator and get himself worked up. So… no, I don’t think I’ve had some period like that.
Have other people told you that you seem emotionally flat or less expressive than you used to?

Um… I don’t think anyone’s said it like that, no. “Flat” sounds kind of… I don’t know, like a robot or something. People have told me I look tired, or that I’m hard to read sometimes, but I’ve kind of always been that way.

My aunt used to say my brother was the dramatic one and I was the one who’d just sit there at family stuff, eating potato salad and not reacting much. But that wasn’t new, you know? So… no, I haven’t really noticed being less expressive than I used to be, and I don’t think anyone’s told me that exactly.
Have you seen things that other people could not see?

Seen things? Like… actually seen something that wasn’t there?

I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes out of the corner of my eye I’ll think somebody moved, but that happens to everybody, right? Like when you’re driving at dusk and a mailbox looks like a person for half a second. I had that happen on my route once near this old bus stop, and it reminded me of when my uncle used to say the road plays tricks on you when you’re tired.

But no, I can’t say I’ve seen things other people couldn’t see.
During this past year, have there been times when other people said your speech was hard to follow or that you were acting in a confused or disorganized way?

Hard to follow? I mean… sometimes people tell me I’m giving too much background. My supervisor says, “Just get to the point,” but he says that to everybody when he’s in one of those moods.

Confused or disorganized… I don’t think so. I mean, work has a lot of steps—routes, checklists, times, little codes—and if you explain it to someone who doesn’t do it, it sounds like a mess. Like my cousin tried to understand my schedule once and thought I was changing topics, but I was explaining why the timing matters.

So… no, I don’t think people have said I’m confused or acting disorganized. Maybe that I talk around things sometimes.
Have you ever believed that your coworkers were secretly recording or monitoring you?

Secretly recording… I don’t know about recording exactly. Monitoring, maybe, yeah. It started after that county safety award, which—honestly, I didn’t even want all the attention from that, because once they put your name up there, people start acting different.

Certain people at work started twisting things in my inspection reports, asking these pointed budget questions like they were trying to make it sound like I was doing something crooked. And my supervisor keeps saying, “It’s just normal review,” but it doesn’t feel normal. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.

It’s like when you turn in a report and then suddenly three people are asking about the same tiny detail, but from different angles. That’s not random. So… secretly recording, I can’t say I saw a recorder or anything, but monitoring me? Yeah, I think that’s been happening.

target_item.manifestation: I’m here because ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked, and even when my supervisor says it’s just normal review, I can tell there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient can consider being mistaken about the belief that coworkers are coordinating against him, which directly assesses the fixed nature of the delusion.

patient.answer:
I mean… I guess anything is possible in the way people say that, but no, I don’t think I’m mistaken about this. Ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked.

And it’s not just one comment, you know? It’s the way it keeps happening. My supervisor keeps saying it’s normal review, but I’ve been doing this job long enough to know when questions are just questions and when they’re part of something. I can tell it’s coordinated. They’re trying to discredit me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the persecutory belief is non-bizarre and encapsulated versus accompanied by broader schizophrenic-spectrum features, helping distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia or acute/organic psychosis.
doctor.question: Outside of this issue at work, have you had any other beliefs that people would find unusual or hard to believe?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked, and even when my supervisor says it’s just normal review, I can tell there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether there are other unusual or hard-to-believe beliefs beyond the workplace concern, which directly relates to the delusions symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, not really. I mean, people might think this work thing sounds hard to believe, but it’s not like I’m coming in here with some wild story about strangers or the news or something.

It’s really just that since I got that county safety award, certain people at work started twisting my inspection reports, asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. And I know my supervisor says it’s normal review, but I’ve been there long enough to know when something feels coordinated.

Outside of that… no, I don’t think there’s anything else like that. It’s this situation at work.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the fixed persecutory belief has mood-incongruent bizarre/Schneiderian psychotic features, which would favor schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis over delusional or paranoid personality pathology.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know what you were thinking?

target_item.reason: The question asks specifically about thought broadcasting, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile; the listed delusion manifestation is about coworkers coordinating to discredit him at work.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. I mean, people can guess what you’re thinking sometimes, especially at work when everyone’s been around each other too long, but that’s not the same thing, right?

Like if I’m sitting in a meeting and somebody knows I’m annoyed, that’s just my face probably. My mom used to say I never hid things well—well, not thoughts, just expressions. But no, I haven’t felt like my thoughts were being, you know, broadcast out loud or sent to people or anything like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether this fixed persecutory belief has been present for at least 3 months, which helps distinguish persistent delusional disorder from acute/transient psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: For at least the past 3 months, have you believed that your coworkers were coordinating against you?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about a year, ever since I got recognized for the county safety initiative.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the belief about coworkers coordinating against him has been present, specifically whether it has lasted at least 3 months.

patient.answer:
Yeah… definitely longer than three months. It’s been about a year, I’d say, since I got recognized for that county safety initiative.

That’s when things started to feel different at work. I remember because everyone was acting congratulatory at first, but then—well, you know how offices get, people smile and then later the tone changes. My cousin had something like that happen when he got promoted at the warehouse, not the same thing exactly, but people get resentful.

So yes, for about a year now I’ve believed they’ve been coordinating against me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have been prominent mood episodes concurrent with the persecutory belief, which would help separate schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis from delusional disorder and other candidates.
doctor.question: During this past year, have you had a period of feeling unusually high, energized, or needing much less sleep than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about manic or hypomanic symptoms, such as elevated energy, unusually high mood, or decreased need for sleep, which are not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… unusually high like happy? I mean, I’ve had days where I’m wound up after work, but anybody would be if they had people picking apart every little thing they do.

Sleep, I guess, has been up and down, but I wouldn’t say I’m suddenly energized like some movie version of it. Sometimes I stay up thinking through things, and then I’m tired the next day. My dad used to do that with bills at the kitchen table—sit there with a calculator and get himself worked up. So… no, I don’t think I’ve had some period like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are any negative symptoms, especially diminished emotional expression, to distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder/paranoid personality.
doctor.question: Have other people told you that you seem emotionally flat or less expressive than you used to?

target_item.reason: The question asks about emotional flatness or reduced expressiveness, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Um… I don’t think anyone’s said it like that, no. “Flat” sounds kind of… I don’t know, like a robot or something. People have told me I look tired, or that I’m hard to read sometimes, but I’ve kind of always been that way.

My aunt used to say my brother was the dramatic one and I was the one who’d just sit there at family stuff, eating potato salad and not reacting much. But that wasn’t new, you know? So… no, I haven’t really noticed being less expressive than I used to be, and I don’t think anyone’s told me that exactly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have been visual hallucinations, which would help distinguish a primary delusional disorder or paranoid personality pattern from schizophrenia-spectrum or organic psychosis.
doctor.question: Have you seen things that other people could not see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about visual hallucinations (seeing things others cannot see), but the provided symptom profile only covers delusions, functioning, impairment, and duration, not hallucinations.

patient.answer:
Seen things? Like… actually seen something that wasn’t there?

I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes out of the corner of my eye I’ll think somebody moved, but that happens to everybody, right? Like when you’re driving at dusk and a mailbox looks like a person for half a second. I had that happen on my route once near this old bus stop, and it reminded me of when my uncle used to say the road plays tricks on you when you’re tired.

But no, I can’t say I’ve seen things other people couldn’t see.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a sustained period of prominent disorganized speech or behavior, which would help distinguish schizophrenia or acute polymorphic psychosis from delusional disorder/paranoid personality traits.
doctor.question: During this past year, have there been times when other people said your speech was hard to follow or that you were acting in a confused or disorganized way?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized speech or behavior, but the provided symptom profile only covers delusions, duration, and functioning-related effects, not confusion or disorganization.

patient.answer:
Hard to follow? I mean… sometimes people tell me I’m giving too much background. My supervisor says, “Just get to the point,” but he says that to everybody when he’s in one of those moods.

Confused or disorganized… I don’t think so. I mean, work has a lot of steps—routes, checklists, times, little codes—and if you explain it to someone who doesn’t do it, it sounds like a mess. Like my cousin tried to understand my schedule once and thought I was changing topics, but I was explaining why the timing matters.

So… no, I don’t think people have said I’m confused or acting disorganized. Maybe that I talk around things sometimes.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the persecutory belief is non-bizarre and circumscribed without broader psychotic symptoms, which would best distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia/paranoid personality disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever believed that your coworkers were secretly recording or monitoring you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked, and even when my supervisor says it’s just normal review, I can tell there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me.
target_item.reason: The question asks about a fixed suspicious belief involving coworkers secretly monitoring or recording him, which is most directly about delusions.

patient.answer:
Secretly recording… I don’t know about recording exactly. Monitoring, maybe, yeah. It started after that county safety award, which—honestly, I didn’t even want all the attention from that, because once they put your name up there, people start acting different.

Certain people at work started twisting things in my inspection reports, asking these pointed budget questions like they were trying to make it sound like I was doing something crooked. And my supervisor keeps saying, “It’s just normal review,” but it doesn’t feel normal. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.

It’s like when you turn in a report and then suddenly three people are asking about the same tiny detail, but from different angles. That’s not random. So… secretly recording, I can’t say I saw a recorder or anything, but monitoring me? Yeah, I think that’s been happening.

inference.note: Ruled out F23.3 because the persecutory belief has been present for about a year, not acute/transient. Persistent, circumscribed workplace persecution delusion with preserved functioning and no clear hallucinations, disorganization, negative symptoms, mania, or widespread suspiciousness makes F22 most likely; F20.0, F60.0, and F06.2 remain differential considerations.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent, circumscribed persecutory delusion focused on coworkers coordinating to discredit and monitor him for about a year. He maintains otherwise intact functioning and denies core schizophrenia features such as hallucinations, thought insertion/broadcasting, disorganization, negative symptoms, or bizarre delusions. There is no evidence of a medical/neurological cause, making delusional disorder, persecutory type, the best fit.
